frame: Rater frame: walk the transaction lifecycle. A binding counts only if another layer or rail can verify it. Connectivity is not interoperability. Recoverability requires a forum and a consequence usable at the commerce seam, not a product that exists somewhere else.

C.promise: Scoped signed mandates (Intent/Cart) as W3C VCs bind authority to payment.
C.evidence: Blog + UCP binding describe tamper-proof VCs and human-present/approval flow.
C.failure: Revocation not consistently propagated into settlement (Ledger L4 open issue).

I.promise: Payment-agnostic (cards, stablecoins, RT bank) and binds to A2A/x402/UCP.
I.evidence: A2A x402 extension named; UCP spec references AP2 mandates; 60+ collaborators.
I.failure: Bindings are one-sided adapters; no cross-rail auditable verification of mandate scope.
I.metric: Count of rails that can independently verify mandate scope at settlement.

A.promise: Auth safety via signed VCs; audit trail intent→cart→payment; pricing in Cart Mandate.
A.evidence: Blog: non-repudiable chain of evidence; human-present WYSIWYP; payment-agnostic.
A.failure: No economic finality guarantee, no compliance continuity, no agent-speed recoverability.
A.metric: 4/7 properties addressed (auth, exec partial, price partial, audit).

EM.promise: Payment-agnostic rails (cards, stablecoins, RT bank) reduce single-institution dependence.
EM.evidence: Blog lists multiple rails; no KYC/ID/court dependency claimed for mandate layer.
EM.failure: Still needs platform trust for dispute; no native remedy where courts/cards weak.
EM.metric: Usable without one institution; fallback required for enforcement.

S.promise: Public GitHub spec, reference implementations, 60+ collaborators; positions as A2A/MCP extension.
S.evidence: spec-ap2 repo + blog announcement; UCP references AP2 mandates.
S.failure: No named governance body or standards-track process; limited independent implementers evidenced.
S.metric: Versioned spec present; governance and multi-vendor adoption not demonstrated.

C.promise: HTTP 402 binds payment proof to resource access; solves L5 payment authorization problem.
C.evidence: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header verified by facilitator; mainnet facilitators (Coinbase CDP, PayAI) settle on-chain.
C.failure: Payment ≠ delivery; no atomic bind of service delivery to finality (T3).
C.metric: Facilitator verifies signature and settles; delivery fidelity unverified.

I.promise: Blockchain-agnostic (EVM, Solana, Algorand); CAIP-2 network IDs; optional Signed Offers/Receipts.
I.evidence: SDKs in TS/Go/Python; middleware (Express, Next, FastAPI); AP2 blog notes A2A x402 extension.
I.failure: Bindings are optional; no auditable cross-layer propagation mandated by base spec.
I.metric: CAIP-2 IDs enable multi-chain; receipts extension not required for interop.

A.promise: Auth safety via signed payment proof; pricing via exact/upto schemes; partial exec/finality/audit.
A.evidence: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE; Permit2 upto; optional receipts; facilitator settlement; compliance receipts are IETF drafts.
A.failure: No native forum; irreversible settlement; compliance/recoverability not deployed.
A.metric: 4 of 7 properties addressed (auth, price, partial exec/finality/audit).

EM.promise: No KYC/accounts; stablecoins; works without cards or banks.
EM.evidence: Zero-friction base flow; blockchain-agnostic SDKs; mainnet facilitators.
EM.failure: Depends on facilitator trust and on-ramp access; no court or fallback for disputes.
EM.metric: Usable without cards/KYC; fails where on-ramps or facilitators are absent.

S.promise: Public spec; Linux Foundation x402 Foundation; multiple independent SDKs and facilitators.
S.evidence: 75.41M tx/30d; members include Stripe, Cloudflare, AWS; IETF drafts for receipts/compliance.
S.failure: Receipts/compliance are drafts; governance is new; no formal standards body process yet.
S.metric: Multiple implementers; Foundation formed 2026; IETF drafts not finalized.

C.promise: L6 lifecycle: catalog, cart, checkout, fulfillment, refund adjustments via order objects and webhooks.
C.evidence: spec-ucp defines order, fulfillment events, adjustments; /.well-known/ucp advertises capabilities.
C.failure: Post-purchase state and refund portability remain merchant-specific (T4).

I.promise: Bindings to AP2 mandates/VCs, A2A agent cards, MCP; OAuth identity linking.
I.evidence: Spec lists AP2, A2A, MCP transports; /.well-known/ucp exposes signing keys and handlers.
I.failure: Bindings are optional/adapter-style; no auditable cross-layer verification of lifecycle state.
I.metric: Another rail verifying UCP order state end-to-end.

A.promise: Auth via OAuth/AP2 VCs; execution via order/fulfillment objects; audit via webhooks/events.
A.evidence: Capabilities include identity linking, order webhooks, refund adjustments; AP2 mandates for payment.
A.failure: No economic finality (PSP/card rail), no compliance continuity, no native recoverability forum.
A.metric: Count of seven properties with observable artifacts.

EM.promise: Reduces dependence on platform trust via open spec and /.well-known discovery.
EM.evidence: REST/MCP/A2A transports; OAuth identity; AP2 payment mandates.
EM.failure: Still requires PSP/card/bank for finality; no fallback where those are absent.

S.promise: Versioned spec with YYYY-MM-DD capability dates; multi-vendor endorsement.
S.evidence: ucp.dev spec overview; GitHub repo; endorsements from Google, Shopify, Stripe, Visa.
S.failure: Lodging/food verticals 'coming soon'; no named independent governance body.

C.promise: Portable identity + behavioral trust registry for L1 adverse selection.
C.evidence: Three registries (identity, reputation, validation) with on-chain summaries and feedback hooks.
C.failure: Identity ≠ capability; Sybil inflation; capability claims not cryptographically guaranteed.
C.metric: getSummary with clientAddresses filter; validation response 0–100.

I.promise: Optional bindings to A2A/MCP/ENS/DID/x402 via registration file.
I.evidence: agentRegistry URIStorage includes endpoints and optional x402Support; feedback MAY include proofOfPayment.
I.failure: Bindings are optional and one-sided; feedback does not bind AP2 mandates or x402 settlement.
I.metric: Presence of endpoint fields in registration file; proofOfPayment hash in feedback.

A.promise: Auditability of feedback and validation; partial recoverability via revocation.
A.evidence: On-chain feedback append/revoke; validation hooks for stakers/zkML/TEE/judges.
A.failure: No authorization safety, execution correctness, economic finality, pricing, or compliance guarantees.

EM.promise: Reduced dependence on platform trust via on-chain reputation.
EM.evidence: Permissionless registry deployment; no KYC/card dependency for registration.
EM.failure: Still requires blockchain access and platform trust for validation; no legal enforcement artifact.
EM.metric: Registry deployability on L2/mainnet; absence of KYC requirement.

S.promise: Public EIP draft with named authors from MetaMask, EF, Google, Coinbase.
S.evidence: EIP-8004 draft status; Magicians thread; no final ratification or multiple independent implementations.
S.failure: Draft status; no versioned governance or canonical mainnet singleton.

C.promise: Tool/data discovery and invocation for AI apps
C.evidence: Capability discovery (prompts, resources, tools) in versioned docs
C.failure: Advertised capability not bound to demonstrated performance (Ledger L2)

I.evidence: Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor listed; UCP uses MCP as transport
I.failure: No binding to payment, mandate, or dispute rails; connectivity ≠ interoperability

A.evidence: trust_model doc; tool-call logs exist per Ledger L3
A.failure: No economic finality, pricing, compliance, or recoverability artifacts

EM.evidence: Web2 origin; no dependency on cards/KYC/courts stated
EM.failure: No artifact for loss-bearer inspection where institutions are weak

S.failure: No named governance body or standards-track process cited

C.promise: L2/L3 discovery + task routing for agent interop
C.evidence: Agent Card JSON schema; Task lifecycle; SDKs in 6 langs
C.failure: Capability claims unbound to demonstrated performance; no competence proof
C.metric: % of advertised skills with verifiable execution trace

I.promise: HTTP/JSON binding; Agent Card URL as cross-layer pointer
I.evidence: UCP uses Agent Card URL; AP2 described as A2A extension; auth in HTTP headers
I.failure: No auditable binding another rail can verify; connectivity ≠ interop
I.metric: Count of external rails that cryptographically verify A2A claims

A.promise: Task traces for message audit; auth declared on Agent Card
A.evidence: Task ID + Message/Part/Artifact log; HTTP-header auth; no payment/finality/recovery
A.failure: No economic finality, pricing, compliance, or recoverability artifacts
A.metric: 4/7 properties addressed (auth partial, exec partial, audit yes)

EM.evidence: REST/SSE/webhooks; no banking or KYC requirement in spec
EM.failure: Still needs platform trust and stable currency; no L8 forum or fallback
EM.metric: Usable without bank/card but not without platform or court

S.promise: Linux Foundation project; TSC with 8 named vendors
S.evidence: Versioned spec at a2a-protocol.org; SDKs in 6 languages; multi-vendor TSC
S.failure: No formal standards-body process (IETF/ISO); governance maturity unclear

C.promise: Stream agent state, UI intents, and user interactions (L7 information revelation).
C.evidence: Event-based protocol with streaming chat, generative UI, shared state, interrupts, and custom events.
C.failure: Interface transparency can hide weaker seams (T5); no binding to settlement or remedy.
C.metric: Event delivery and UI render; no checkable metric for information fidelity beyond presentation.

I.promise: Framework and SDK integrations (LangGraph, CrewAI, ADK, etc.) for agent↔user connectivity.
I.evidence: Integration table on docs site; SDKs in Kotlin, Go, Dart, Java, Rust.
I.failure: Connectivity without cross-layer propagation; no auditable binding to L4/L5/L8 rails.
I.metric: Number of integrations; no verifiable cross-seam guarantee.

A.promise: Observability via streaming events and HITL interrupts.
A.evidence: Docs describe thinking-step visualization, interrupts (pause, approve, edit, retry), and custom events.
A.failure: No mandate, settlement, pricing, compliance, or dispute objects; auditability is partial (UI events only).
A.metric: Event log exists but does not reconstruct economic flow or authorization scope.

EM.evidence: No artifacts for banking access, legal enforcement, formal ID, platform trust, or currency stability.
EM.failure: Depends on platform and framework stack; no fallback for missing institutions.
EM.metric: No usable metric for loss-bearer inspection in emerging markets.

S.promise: Open protocol with versioned docs and multiple independent SDKs.
S.evidence: GitHub repo, docs site, SDKs in 5+ languages, integrations with major agent frameworks.
S.failure: Originated from single vendor (CopilotKit); governance and independent adoption not fully documented.
S.metric: SDK count and integration table; no standards body process.

C.promise: L8 contract enforcement: forum, rules, and consequence for disputes.
C.evidence: ERC-792 Arbitrator/Arbitrable split; crowdsourced jurors stake PNK, vote, appeal hierarchy.
C.failure: Resolution is days-scale, not agent-speed; not wired as default L8 for AP2/x402/UCP.
C.metric: Dispute resolved with binding consequence; latency days vs required agent-speed.

I.promise: Arbitrable contracts can call Kleros; evidence via ERC-1497.
I.evidence: Escrow product integrates Kleros; one OA record shows sneaker escrow + Kleros.
I.failure: No specified binding to AP2/x402/UCP rails; connectivity ≠ interoperability.
I.metric: Count of L4–L7 protocols with auditable Kleros binding as default dispute layer.

A.promise: Auditability of evidence; recoverability via arbitration ruling.
A.evidence: ERC-1497 evidence submission; on-chain votes, appeals, rulings; escrow holds funds.
A.failure: Authorization, execution, pricing, economic finality, compliance not addressed by Kleros itself.
A.metric: 3 of 7 properties addressed (auditability yes; recoverability partial; others no).

EM.promise: Dispute resolution without reliance on courts or card networks.
EM.evidence: On-chain arbitration usable where courts are weak; PNK-staked jurors; global access.
EM.failure: Requires crypto banking access and PNK liquidity; enforcement across jurisdictions not automatic.
EM.metric: Usable without court/card; fails if no on-ramp or cross-border recognition.

S.promise: Versioned ERC-792/ERC-1497 specs; cooperative governance; live since 2019.
S.evidence: Multiple products (Court, Escrow, Curate, PoH); Snapshot governance; Stanford JBLP article.
S.failure: No formal standards-body process; limited independent L8 implementations for agentic commerce.
S.metric: ERC status; number of independent arbitrable implementations; governance artifacts.
